gaps.why_now: Phase 11 now has multiple bounded starters that touch watchdog and hvc surfaces, so one shared note keeps the public-header boundary explicit instead of leaving reviewers to infer that UAPI and shared core ownership still remain outside the tranche.

A dedicated shared survey gate now verifies that the Phase 11 note, the watchdog headers, the hvc header, the shared build inventory, and the driver-local survey packets all still describe the same bounded public-header posture and exact shared-versus-dedicated replay contract.

The dw_wdt lane now records that `include/uapi/linux/watchdog.h` still owns `struct watchdog_info` plus the `WDIOC_*` and `WDIOF_*` or `WDIOS_*` surface, while `include/linux/watchdog.h` still owns `watchdog_device` and `watchdog_ops` so the DesignWare starter does not overclaim watchdog parity.

The hvc_console starter already carries a tiny header-parity snapshot for `drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_console.h` that mirrors `MAX_NR_HVC_CONSOLES`, `HVC_ALLOC_TTY_ADAPTERS`, the `hv_ops` callback shape, `hvc_kick()`, the default `notifier_*_irq()` helper exports, and exported hvc helper metadata without widening into tty registration or host-backed I/O.

The shared header-parity gate now replays the `hvc_console.zig` header snapshot directly, and it also checks that the dedicated hvc archival survey still carries the `struct winsize` layout, `struct hv_ops` layout, and bounded `hv_ops` callback-signature proofs, so the mirrored console-limit constants, exported hvc helper surface, default `notifier_*_irq()` helper exports, and `hv_ops` callback booleans remain machine-checked instead of living only in prose.

The shared header-parity gate now carries one bounded `layout_assert` checkpoint for `struct watchdog_info` so size, alignment, exact field types, and field offsets stay reviewable without turning this simple-driver slice into a wider watchdog-core ownership claim.

The shared header-parity gate now carries one bounded `layout_assert` checkpoint for `struct winsize` so the hvc resize surface keeps size, alignment, exact field types, and `ws_row` or `ws_col` or `ws_xpixel` or `ws_ypixel` offsets reviewable without claiming tty-core or `struct hvc_struct` ownership.

The shared header-parity gate now carries one bounded exported-helper signature checkpoint for `hvc_instantiate()`, `hvc_alloc()`, `hvc_remove()`, `hvc_poll()`, `hvc_kick()`, `__hvc_resize()`, and the default `notifier_*_irq()` helpers so the C calling convention and `struct winsize` resize handoff stay machine-checked without claiming tty-core, notifier execution, or host-backed I/O ownership.

If a later Phase 11 driver begins mirroring public-header constants or shared struct layouts beyond these bounded snapshots, the honest next step is a driver-local checkpoint plus an explicit handoff to the Phase 3 interop substrate rather than a silent simple-driver parity claim.
